course.title: Sleep and Recovery
course.tagline: Sleep deeply and recover properly, with routines that actually work.

days.title: Why sleep matters
days.goal: Learn why sleep is not wasted time.

video.title: 10 Easy Ways to Improve Your Sleep

steps: Watch the video and write the main idea in one sentence.
Learn this: sleep repairs the body and clears the mind.
Write down how many hours you slept last night.
Set a sleep goal: 7 to 8 hours a night.
days.task: Write your sleep hours from last night.
days.challenge: Tell a friend why sleep matters in one sentence.

quiz.q: Why does sleep matter?
options: It repairs the body and clears the mind
quiz.explain: Sleep is when the body repairs itself.

quiz.q: How much sleep should an adult aim for?
quiz.explain: Seven to eight hours is the healthy aim.

quiz.q: What should you write down first?
quiz.explain: Knowing your sleep hours shows where to improve.

days.title: Set your sleep times
days.goal: Pick a bedtime and a wake time and keep them.

video.title: 8 Hours of Sleep and Still Exhausted? Fix It FAST Tonight

steps: Pick a wake time that fits your day.
Count back 8 hours to find your bedtime.
Write both times on a card by your bed.
Keep the same times even on weekends.
days.task: Write your bedtime and wake time on a card.
days.challenge: Keep the same times for 3 days.

quiz.q: Why keep the same sleep times?
options: It is a rule with no reason
quiz.explain: Same times train the body to sleep and wake easily.

quiz.q: How do you find your bedtime?
options: Count back 8 hours from your wake time
quiz.explain: Counting back gives you enough sleep.

quiz.q: What about weekends?
quiz.explain: Same times on weekends keep the rhythm steady.

days.title: Your bedroom: dark, cool, quiet
days.goal: Make your bedroom a good place to sleep.

video.title: Muscle Recovery Process & Tips

steps: Make the room dark: close curtains or wear a sleep mask.
Make the room cool: open a window or use a fan.
Make the room quiet: turn off noisy things.
Keep your bed only for sleep.
days.task: Make one change to your bedroom tonight.
days.challenge: Make your room dark, cool and quiet tonight.

quiz.q: Why should the room be dark?
options: Darkness tells the brain it is time to sleep
quiz.explain: Darkness helps the sleep hormone work.

quiz.q: Why should the room be cool?
options: A cool room helps you fall asleep
quiz.explain: A cool room helps deep sleep.

quiz.q: Why keep the bed only for sleep?
options: It is a rule with no reason
So your brain links bed with sleep
quiz.explain: Bed only for sleep trains the brain.

days.title: Wind down: 30 minutes before bed
days.goal: Learn a simple wind-down routine.

video.title: Sleep

steps: 30 minutes before bed, dim the lights.
Put your phone away and charge it outside the bedroom.
Read a book or listen to calm music.
Do 5 slow breaths.
days.task: Do the wind-down routine tonight.
days.challenge: Do it every night this week.

quiz.q: Why wind down before bed?
options: It tells the body the day is over
quiz.explain: Winding down prepares the body for sleep.

quiz.q: What should you do with your phone?
options: Put it away and charge it outside the bedroom
quiz.explain: Phones keep the brain awake.

quiz.q: How long should a wind-down be?
quiz.explain: Thirty minutes is enough to calm down.

days.title: Caffeine and sleep
days.goal: Learn how coffee and tea affect sleep.

video.title: Sleep Like a Champ

steps: Caffeine is the wake-up chemical in coffee, tea and cola.
It can stay in your body for 6 hours or more.
Stop caffeine by 2 pm.
Drink water or herbal tea after 2 pm.
days.task: Stop caffeine after 2 pm today.
days.challenge: Drink water instead of coffee this afternoon.

quiz.q: What is caffeine?
options: The wake-up chemical in coffee, tea and cola
quiz.explain: Caffeine keeps you awake.

quiz.q: How long does caffeine stay in the body?
quiz.explain: Caffeine lingers for hours.

quiz.q: When should you stop caffeine?
quiz.explain: Stopping by 2 pm lets it clear before bed.

days.title: Move in the day, sleep at night
days.goal: Learn how daytime movement helps night sleep.

video.title: 5 Night Habits for Better Sleep | Simple Wellness Routine for Restful Nights

steps: Walk or exercise for 30 minutes today.
Finish hard exercise at least 3 hours before bed.
Get sunlight in the morning if you can.
Write down how you slept after moving.
days.task: Walk for 30 minutes today.
days.challenge: Get morning sunlight for 10 minutes.

quiz.q: Why does daytime movement help sleep?
options: It tires the body in a healthy way
quiz.explain: Daytime movement builds healthy tiredness.

quiz.q: When should you finish hard exercise?
quiz.explain: Late hard exercise keeps you awake.

quiz.q: Why get morning sunlight?
options: It sets your body clock for the day
quiz.explain: Morning light tells the body when to wake and sleep.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 1: Your sleep diary
days.goal: Put week 1 together: keep a sleep diary for 3 nights.

video.title: 6 tips for better sleep | Sleeping with Science, a TED series

steps: Each morning, write: bedtime, wake time, hours slept.
Rate your sleep: good, OK or bad.
Note one thing that helped or hurt your sleep.
Find one pattern in your diary.
days.task: Keep a sleep diary for 3 nights.
days.challenge: Find one pattern in your diary.

quiz.q: What is a sleep diary?
options: A written record of your sleep each night
quiz.explain: A diary shows your sleep patterns.

quiz.q: What should you write each morning?
options: Bedtime, wake time and hours slept
quiz.explain: Times and hours show your sleep pattern.

quiz.q: Why find patterns?
options: So you can fix what hurts sleep
quiz.explain: Patterns show what to change.

project.title: Your sleep diary
project.brief: Keep a sleep diary for 3 nights: bedtime, wake time, hours slept, a rating, and one note on what helped or hurt.
checks: Each night has bedtime and wake time
Notes on help and hurt are included

days.title: Breathe to fall asleep
days.goal: Learn slow breathing that helps you drift off.

video.title: 18-Minute Movement Medicine

steps: Lie down and close your eyes.
Breathe in for 4 counts, out for 6 counts.
Do this 10 times.
Let your body go soft with each out-breath.
days.task: Do 10 slow breaths in bed tonight.
days.challenge: Use slow breathing if you wake up at night.

quiz.q: How should you breathe to fall asleep?
quiz.explain: A long out-breath calms the body.

quiz.q: Why breathe slowly in bed?
options: It slows the heart and relaxes muscles
quiz.explain: Slow breathing tells the body it is safe to sleep.

quiz.q: What should you do if you wake up at night?
quiz.explain: Slow breathing helps you drift back off.

days.title: What to eat and drink for sleep
days.goal: Learn simple food rules for better sleep.

video.title: Essentials: Sleep Toolkit for Optimizing Sleep & Sleep-Wake Timing

steps: Do not eat a heavy meal close to bedtime.
A small snack like a banana is fine.
Avoid alcohol before bed: it breaks your sleep.
Drink water through the day, less at night.
days.task: Eat a light dinner tonight.
days.challenge: Drink less water in the last hour before bed.

quiz.q: Why not eat a heavy meal before bed?
quiz.explain: A heavy meal keeps the body working at night.

quiz.q: Why avoid alcohol before bed?
options: It breaks your sleep into pieces
quiz.explain: Alcohol stops deep sleep.

quiz.q: What is a good bedtime snack?
quiz.explain: A small snack is fine; a big meal is not.

days.title: Naps: short and early
days.goal: Learn how to nap without ruining night sleep.

video.title: Sleep Toolkit: Tools for Optimizing Sleep & Sleep-Wake Timing | Huberman Lab Podcast #84

steps: Keep naps under 30 minutes.
Nap before 3 pm.
Set an alarm so you do not oversleep.
If you sleep well at night, you may not need naps.
days.task: Take a 20-minute nap before 3 pm if you are tired.
days.challenge: Set an alarm for your nap.

quiz.q: How long should a nap be?
quiz.explain: A short nap refreshes without stealing night sleep.

quiz.q: When should you nap?
quiz.explain: Early naps do not hurt night sleep.

quiz.q: Why set an alarm for a nap?
quiz.explain: An alarm keeps the nap short.

days.title: Stretch before bed
days.goal: Learn gentle stretches that help you sleep.

video.title: 10 Easy Ways to Improve Your Sleep

steps: Lie on your back and hug your knees to your chest.
Do a gentle twist on each side.
Stretch your arms up high and breathe out.
Do this for 5 minutes before bed.
days.task: Do the bedtime stretches tonight.
days.challenge: Do them every night this week.

quiz.q: Why stretch before bed?
quiz.explain: Gentle stretches ease the body into sleep.

quiz.q: How long should you stretch?
quiz.explain: Five minutes is enough to relax.

quiz.q: How should stretches feel?
quiz.explain: Gentle stretches are safe.

days.title: When you cannot fall asleep
days.goal: Learn what to do when sleep will not come.

video.title: 8 Hours of Sleep and Still Exhausted? Fix It FAST Tonight

steps: If you cannot sleep after 20 minutes, get up.
Go to another room and do something calm: read a book.
Do not check your phone.
Go back to bed when you feel sleepy.
days.task: Use the get-up rule tonight if you cannot sleep.
days.challenge: Read a book instead of your phone tonight.

quiz.q: What should you do if you cannot sleep?
options: Get up after 20 minutes and do something calm
quiz.explain: Getting up breaks the worry cycle.

quiz.q: Why not check your phone?
options: Bright screens wake the brain up
quiz.explain: Phone light tells the brain to stay awake.

quiz.q: What is a good calm activity?
quiz.explain: A calm book helps sleepiness return.

days.title: Recovery: rest your muscles
days.goal: Learn how muscles recover after training.

video.title: Muscle Recovery Process & Tips

steps: After training, walk slowly for 5 minutes.
Stretch gently for 5 minutes.
Drink water and eat protein.
Sleep 7 to 9 hours to repair muscles.
days.task: Do a 5-minute cool-down after your next workout.
days.challenge: Eat protein after training today.

quiz.q: Why cool down after training?
options: It helps muscles relax and recover
quiz.explain: A cool-down eases the body back to rest.

quiz.q: Why eat protein after training?
quiz.explain: Protein is the repair material for muscle.

quiz.q: How much sleep helps recovery?
quiz.explain: Seven to nine hours repairs muscles.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 2: Your bedtime routine
days.goal: Put week 2 together: build your own bedtime routine.

video.title: Sleep

steps: Write your routine: dim lights, phone away, stretch, breathe, sleep.
Do the routine every night for 3 nights.
Write down how you slept each morning.
Fix one thing that did not work.
days.task: Write your bedtime routine.
days.challenge: Follow it for 3 nights.

quiz.q: What should a bedtime routine have?
options: Dim lights, phone away, stretch, breathe
quiz.explain: A calm routine tells the body it is bedtime.

quiz.q: Why follow it for 3 nights?
options: To see if it helps before changing it
quiz.explain: Three nights shows if the routine works.

quiz.q: What should you do if a step does not help?
options: Swap it for another calm step
quiz.explain: Swapping keeps the routine working for you.

project.title: Your bedtime routine
project.brief: Build your own bedtime routine: dim lights, phone away, stretch, breathe, sleep, and follow it for 3 nights.
checks: Fixed one thing that did not work

days.title: Rest days and active recovery
days.goal: Learn the difference between rest and active recovery.

video.title: Sleep Like a Champ

steps: Rest means no hard training.
Active recovery means gentle movement: walking, stretching, easy yoga.
Take 2 rest days a week.
On rest days, walk for 20 minutes.
days.task: Take a rest day today and walk for 20 minutes.
days.challenge: Do gentle yoga on your rest day.

quiz.q: What is active recovery?
options: Gentle movement on a rest day
quiz.explain: Gentle movement helps the body recover.

quiz.q: How many rest days should you take?
quiz.explain: Two rest days let the body repair.

quiz.q: What is a good rest-day activity?
quiz.explain: A gentle walk aids recovery.

days.title: Deal with snoring and noise
days.goal: Learn simple fixes for a noisy bedroom.

video.title: 5 Night Habits for Better Sleep | Simple Wellness Routine for Restful Nights

steps: Use earplugs if noise wakes you.
Use a fan for steady background sound.
Ask a snoring partner to sleep on their side.
Keep the room cool and dark.
days.task: Try earplugs or a fan tonight.
days.challenge: Ask your partner to try sleeping on their side.

quiz.q: What helps with bedroom noise?
quiz.explain: Earplugs or steady sound block noise.

quiz.q: Why does a fan help?
options: Its steady sound masks sudden noises
quiz.explain: Steady sound hides sudden noises.

quiz.q: What helps a snoring partner?
quiz.explain: Side sleeping often eases snoring.

days.title: Morning light and your body clock
days.goal: Learn how morning light sets your sleep.

video.title: 6 tips for better sleep | Sleeping with Science, a TED series

steps: Get outside for 10 minutes in the morning.
Open your curtains as soon as you wake up.
Eat breakfast near a window.
Write down how awake you felt.
days.task: Get 10 minutes of morning light tomorrow.
days.challenge: Open your curtains first thing tomorrow.

quiz.q: Why get morning light?
options: It sets your body clock for the day
quiz.explain: Morning light tells the body when to wake and sleep.

quiz.q: How much morning light helps?
quiz.explain: Ten minutes of light sets the clock.

quiz.q: What should you do first in the morning?
options: Check your phone in the dark
quiz.explain: Light first thing wakes the body up.

days.title: Track your sleep for a week
days.goal: Keep a full week of sleep records.

video.title: 18-Minute Movement Medicine

steps: Write bedtime, wake time and hours slept each day.
Rate each night: good, OK or bad.
Note what helped or hurt each night.
Find your best and worst nights.
days.task: Keep your sleep diary for 7 nights.
days.challenge: Find your best night and what made it good.

quiz.q: Why track sleep for a week?
quiz.explain: A week of records shows what works.

quiz.q: What should you note each night?
options: What helped or hurt your sleep
quiz.explain: Notes show what to keep and what to fix.

quiz.q: What should you do with your best night?
quiz.explain: Repeating what worked builds better sleep.

days.title: Handle a bad night
days.goal: Learn what to do after a night of poor sleep.

video.title: Essentials: Sleep Toolkit for Optimizing Sleep & Sleep-Wake Timing

steps: Do not panic: one bad night is normal.
Get morning light and move gently.
Do not nap too long or too late.
Go to bed at your normal time tonight.
days.task: Get morning light after a bad night.
days.challenge: Keep your normal bedtime after a bad night.

quiz.q: Is one bad night a problem?
quiz.explain: One bad night happens to everyone.

quiz.q: What should you do after a bad night?
options: Get light, move gently, keep your bedtime
quiz.explain: Light and routine reset the body clock.

quiz.q: Why keep your normal bedtime?
options: It keeps your body clock steady
quiz.explain: A steady bedtime fixes the rhythm.

days.title: Relax your mind before bed
days.goal: Learn a simple way to quiet a busy mind.

video.title: Sleep Toolkit: Tools for Optimizing Sleep & Sleep-Wake Timing | Huberman Lab Podcast #84

steps: Write your worries on paper before bed.
Write one thing you will do about each worry tomorrow.
Close the notebook and put it away.
Breathe slowly for 2 minutes.
days.task: Write your worries down tonight before bed.
days.challenge: Close the notebook and breathe slowly.

quiz.q: Why write worries down?
options: It stops them spinning in your head
quiz.explain: Writing worries down makes them smaller.

quiz.q: What should you write next to each worry?
quiz.explain: A small step turns worry into a plan.

quiz.q: Why close the notebook?
options: It tells your mind the day is done
quiz.explain: Closing the book signals rest.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 3: Your sleep system
days.goal: Put week 3 together: build a sleep system you can keep.

video.title: 10 Easy Ways to Improve Your Sleep

steps: Write your sleep times, your wind-down and your bedroom setup.
Add your morning light habit.
Follow the system for 7 nights.
Write down your average hours slept.
days.task: Write your sleep system on one page.
days.challenge: Follow it for 7 nights.

quiz.q: What should a sleep system have?
options: Sleep times, wind-down, bedroom setup and morning light
quiz.explain: A system covers the whole day.

quiz.q: Why follow it for 7 nights?
options: A week shows if the system works
quiz.explain: A week of practice shows real change.

quiz.q: What should you measure?
quiz.explain: Average hours show if the system works.

project.title: Your sleep system
project.brief: Build a sleep system: sleep times, wind-down, bedroom setup and morning light, and follow it for 7 nights.

days.title: Teach a friend to sleep better
days.goal: Teach someone else what helped your sleep.

video.title: 8 Hours of Sleep and Still Exhausted? Fix It FAST Tonight

steps: Show them your sleep diary.
Teach them the wind-down routine.
Teach them slow breathing in bed.
Ask them how they slept after trying it.
days.task: Teach slow breathing to one person.
days.challenge: Show a friend your wind-down routine.

quiz.q: Why teach someone else?
options: Teaching helps you learn it better
quiz.explain: Teaching locks in your own learning.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to teach?
quiz.explain: A wind-down is simple and works fast.

quiz.q: Why ask how they slept?
options: So you know if the tips helped
quiz.explain: Feedback shows what works.

days.title: Review your month
days.goal: Look back at your month of sleep work.

video.title: Muscle Recovery Process & Tips

steps: Read your sleep diary from weeks 1 to 3.
List 3 things that helped your sleep most.
List 1 thing that is still hard.
Write one fix for the hard thing.
days.task: List 3 things that helped your sleep most.
days.challenge: Fix one hard thing in your system.

quiz.q: Why review your month?
options: To see what helped and what needs fixing
quiz.explain: Reviewing shows real progress.

quiz.q: What should you do with a hard thing?
options: Fix it with one small change
quiz.explain: One small fix keeps the system going.

quiz.q: What is a sign your sleep is better?
options: You wake up feeling rested more often
quiz.explain: Waking rested more often means it works.

days.title: Keep your sleep for life
days.goal: Make good sleep a habit for life.

video.title: Sleep

steps: Keep your sleep times, even on holidays.
Keep your wind-down routine.
Keep your bedroom dark, cool and quiet.
Check your sleep diary once a month.
days.task: Keep your sleep times this weekend.
days.challenge: Check your sleep diary once this month.

quiz.q: How do you keep good sleep for life?
quiz.explain: Steady habits keep sleep good.

quiz.q: Why keep times on holidays?
quiz.explain: Steady times keep the rhythm strong.

quiz.q: How often should you check your diary?
quiz.explain: Monthly checks catch problems early.

days.title: Sounds that help you sleep
days.goal: Learn which sounds help you sleep.

video.title: Sleep Like a Champ

steps: Try soft rain sounds or calm music.
Keep the volume low.
Use a timer to stop the sound after 30 minutes.
Avoid loud or exciting music.
Test one sound for 3 nights.
Keep the sound that works best.
days.task: Try a sleep sound tonight.
days.challenge: Use the same sound for 3 nights.

quiz.q: What kind of sound helps sleep?
quiz.explain: Soft calm sounds relax the mind.

quiz.q: Why use a timer?
options: So the sound stops after you fall asleep
quiz.explain: A timer saves battery and stops the sound waking you.

quiz.q: How many nights should you test a sound?
quiz.explain: Three nights shows if a sound really helps.

days.title: Recover after a hard workout
days.goal: Learn how to recover well after hard exercise.

video.title: 5 Night Habits for Better Sleep | Simple Wellness Routine for Restful Nights

steps: Walk slowly for 5 minutes after training.
Drink water.
Eat a meal with protein within 2 hours.
Stretch gently.
Sleep well that night.
Take a rest day the next day.
days.task: Do the recovery steps after your next workout.
days.challenge: Take a full rest day after a hard workout.

quiz.q: What should you do right after training?
quiz.explain: A slow walk cools the body down gently.

quiz.q: When should you eat after training?
quiz.explain: Eating within 2 hours helps muscles repair.

quiz.q: Why take a rest day?
options: Muscles grow and repair when you rest
quiz.explain: Rest is when muscles rebuild stronger.

days.title: Reset after a bad night
days.goal: Learn what to do after one bad night of sleep.

video.title: 6 tips for better sleep | Sleeping with Science, a TED series

steps: Get up at your normal time.
Go outside for morning light.
Drink water and eat a simple breakfast.
Take a short nap of 20 minutes if you must.
Avoid caffeine after lunch.
Go to bed at your normal time.
days.task: Write your bad-night plan.
days.challenge: Follow the plan after your next bad night.

quiz.q: What should you do after a bad night?
options: Get up at your normal time
quiz.explain: A normal wake time keeps your body clock steady.

quiz.q: How long should a nap be?
quiz.explain: A 20-minute nap refreshes you without ruining the night.

quiz.q: When should you go to bed?
quiz.explain: A normal bedtime keeps your sleep pattern steady.

days.title: Get ready for your capstone
days.goal: Review the whole course and prepare your final project.

video.title: 18-Minute Movement Medicine

steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 4.
List 5 things you learned about sleep.
Practise your capstone routine once.
Write down any questions you still have.
days.task: List 5 things you learned in this course.
days.challenge: Do your capstone routine from memory.

quiz.q: What is the capstone?
options: A final project that shows what you learned
quiz.explain: The capstone is your final show of skill.

quiz.q: What should you review before the capstone?
options: Your notes from all four weeks
quiz.explain: Reviewing all weeks brings the course together.

quiz.q: How do you know you are ready?
options: You can follow your sleep system for a week
quiz.explain: A week of good sleep shows you are ready.

days.title: Final practice day
days.goal: Practise your capstone once more, then rest.

video.title: Essentials: Sleep Toolkit for Optimizing Sleep & Sleep-Wake Timing

steps: Do your capstone routine one more time.
Check your sleep system is written down.
Fix anything that felt hard.
Rest well tonight.
days.task: Run your capstone routine tonight.
days.challenge: Fix one hard part of your system.

quiz.q: Why practise once more?
options: Practice makes the real run calm and smooth
quiz.explain: Practice turns worry into calm confidence.

quiz.q: What should you check after practice?
options: Your routine, your times and your bedroom
quiz.explain: Checking your routine makes it smooth.

quiz.q: What should you do the night before?
quiz.explain: Good rest helps you do your best.

days.title: Capstone day: your sleep system
days.goal: Show what you learned: present your sleep system and follow it for a week.

video.title: Sleep Toolkit: Tools for Optimizing Sleep & Sleep-Wake Timing | Huberman Lab Podcast #84

steps: Show your sleep system: times, wind-down, bedroom, morning light.
Show your sleep diary from the week.
Explain your system in simple words.
Write a short report on your month.
days.task: Present your system, show your diary and write your report.
days.challenge: Hand in your report and celebrate.

quiz.q: What should your system show?
options: Times, wind-down, bedroom and morning light
quiz.explain: A full system shows real skill.

quiz.q: What should your diary show?
options: A week of sleep times and ratings
quiz.explain: A week diary proves the system works.

quiz.q: What goes in your report?
options: What you did and what you learned
quiz.explain: A short report shows what you learned.

capstone.title: Your sleep system
capstone.brief: Present your sleep system, show a week of sleep diary records, explain the system in simple words, and write a short report on your month.
checks: Showed a week of diary records
deliverables: A week of sleep diary records
A list of sleep tips learned
A short video or notes from teaching
